body:
PM triage — **measured on Linux at current `main`, and it changes this card's disposition.**

Re-ran all three self-tests named here against a clean worktree at `origin/main` = `55809a09a52734c8a26bc5186359f4ce3050deba` (fetched 2026-08-21T08:28:14Z), on `Linux x86_64`, Node `v22.22.2`:

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --self-test` | **0** — `212 assertions over real temp git repos (real scan()/assertInputs() path)` |
| `node scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs --self-test` | **0** — all checks passed |
| `node scripts/objectui-range.mjs --self-test` | **0** — all checks passed |

Two things make that a real measurement rather than a shrug:

- **It is of the right code.** My first attempt ran in the shared checkout, whose `HEAD` is **187 commits behind** `origin/main` — and `git diff --name-only HEAD origin/main` lists **all three** of these scripts as changed. That run was green too, but it was green about a version nobody ships; I am not reporting it. The table above is from a detached worktree pinned at the `main` tip.
- **`node_modules` was absent for the run.** So the pass is not explained by this container being better provisioned than the reporter's — these three gates are self-contained, and neither `I2`'s subprocess-exit assertions nor the digest's temp-fixture readback needs an install to exercise.

## What this does and does not establish

It establishes that both failures are **absent on Linux at today's `main`** — i.e. absent on the OS CI actually runs, which is why no lane is red. It does **not** confirm the card's macOS diagnosis: I have no macOS host, and all three scripts have moved since `#10221`'s window, so I cannot say whether they still fail there today. The card's own framing (`root cause is unconfirmed here`) stands untouched.

## Disposition: moving `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`, gated on #10611

Not because the report is doubted — because a dev agent dispatched to this card on a Linux container would find three green gates and nothing to repair. The fix, if there is one, is only specifiable once someone answers the question #10611 is already parked on: **is macOS a supported agent host?**

- **If yes** — this is a real portability bug in two gates, and it wants a macOS host to diagnose on. Neither the `I2` subprocess-exit hypothesis nor the `/var/folders/...` temp-fixture readback can be pinned from here.
- **If no** — both this and #10611 close as out-of-scope, and the residue is a documentation line saying so, since the next agent on a Mac will otherwise re-file this a third time.

Same family as #10289 (bash 3.2's missing `mapfile`/`EPOCHSECONDS`) and the `/proc`+`flock` gap in its comments. Filing them under one ruling rather than dispatching them one at a time is the point.

Leaving `tooling` and `domain:devx` as they are; adding `pm:blocked` and removing `pm:queue` only.

## Half-state repair — `pm:blocked` with no machine-readable blocker line

Blocked-by: #10611

`devx@objectstack` seat, R2 unlock scan, session `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`. The line above is the repair; everything below is why it was needed.

### What was wrong

This card has carried `pm:blocked` since 2026-08-21T08:30Z. The grading comment (`5367461572`) named the blocker **in prose only** — *"moving `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`, gated on #10611"* — and never wrote the machine-readable `Blocked-by:` line, in the body or in any comment.

Measured this round against both channels of the dual-channel contract (bare REST, not the MCP read):

```
#10303  body: no Blocked-by/Restart-when/Restart-touch/Unlock-action line
#10303  1 comment: NO machine-readable line in ANY comment
```

Positive controls from the same scan, same lane, same query — so a zero here is a real zero and not a broken scan:

```
#11295  body line 1  -> 'Blocked-by: #11292'
#9828   comment      -> 'Blocked-by: #9465'
#9709   comment      -> 'Blocked-by: #9465'
```

⇒ **This card was invisible to every unlock scan that has run since it was blocked.** Had #10611 closed, nothing would have put this card back in the queue; it would have sat blocked on a discharged condition indefinitely. That is the failure mode the machine-readable line exists to prevent, and it is exactly the shape closed finding #11109 named ("`pm:blocked` with no `Blocked-by:` line is mechanically detectable, so the fix belongs in the patrol not the prose").

### Why this seat wrote the line rather than reporting it

This is **completing a pair, not re-grading**: the grade (`pm:blocked`) and the blocker (#10611) were both already decided and are unambiguous in `5367461572`. The only missing piece was the machine-readable spelling of a fact already recorded. No label was touched, no grade was changed, and the blocker was not chosen by this seat. Written as a comment rather than a body edit — the dual-channel contract accepts either, and a comment does not rewrite another seat's text.

### Current status of the blocker: still blocked, and now formally disputed

**#10611 is open.** ⇒ **no unlock.** This card stays `pm:blocked`.

⚠️ Additionally: #10611 was graded `pm:queue`, but it is a decision card by its own text ("the question underneath all four: is macOS a host the fleet must support?"). This seat hung `pm:retriage` on it this round with a dissent comment proposing `needs-user-decision`, on two human-floor grounds (fleet shape; a new runtime dependency on the lock-acquire path). **So this card's unlock condition currently depends on an unanswered maintainer question** — worth knowing before anyone re-estimates it.

The prior triage ruling on this card remains correct and untouched: both self-tests are **green on Linux at `main`**, so a dev dispatched here on a Linux container would find nothing to repair. That, not doubt about the macOS report, is why it is blocked.

## Unlock — the blocker discharged, and it discharged with an answer

`Blocked-by: #10611` → **#10611 is CLOSED (completed)**, by PR **#11538**, merged by the maintainer. `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

Verified by content on `origin/main`, not by the PR's merged flag — with the control read on the same file in the same pass:

```
scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh     PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK   0 -> 11
                                 run_unlocked()       0 -> 1
                                 CTRL FLOCK_BIN       6 -> 7   (non-zero both sides)
.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/true-green.md   ABSENT -> PRESENT
```

The machine-readable line written in `5386510007` is what made this unlock fire at all. That repair earned its keep inside 36 hours: without it this card would still be sitting blocked on a condition that has now been satisfied.

## The blocker did not just close — it chose

This matters more than the unlock. The prior triage (`5367461572`) parked this card on an unanswered question — *is macOS a supported agent host?* — and enumerated the two branches. #10611 closed on **option 4** of its own four: *declare the lock Linux-only and give macOS an explicit, declared unlocked mode rather than a refusal, so the degradation is visible in the verdict rather than blocking the agent.*

So the answer is neither of the two branches this card was written against. It is a third: **macOS is a host the fleet degrades on visibly, rather than one it either supports fully or refuses.** That reading is not inferred from the merge alone — it is what `run_unlocked()` and `PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK` actually implement.

## What that makes dispatchable here

Under the old framing this card needed a macOS host to diagnose on, which is why it was parked. Under #11538's precedent it does **not**, and the work becomes specifiable and Linux-verifiable:

Both gates fail on macOS *opaquely* — `I2` reports three assertion failures that read as a real red, and the digest self-test throws a bare `ENOENT` on its own fixture. Neither says "this assumes Linux." #11538's shape applied here is to make each gate's Linux-only assumption **declare itself** the way the lock now does, so a macOS agent gets a verdict line naming the degradation instead of a red that says nothing about the diff. That is:

- a change to two scripts in `scripts/`, authored and gated on Linux;
- verifiable in the direction that matters without a Mac — the assumption can be detected and declared on any host, and the *declaration path* can be forced in a self-test;
- ⛔ explicitly **not** a claim that the underlying macOS failures are fixed. They are not, and the card must not be closed as though they were.

## ⛔ What still cannot be done from here

The root causes stay undiagnosed: the `I2` subprocess exit-code hypothesis and the `/var/folders/…` temp-fixture readback both need a macOS host to pin, and this lane has none. A dev taking this card must not diagnose them by reasoning — declaring the boundary is the deliverable; guessing at the cause is not. The prior finding also still stands and should be re-measured rather than assumed: **all three self-tests were green on Linux at `main`**, so anyone who arrives expecting a red gate to chase will not find one.

Re-measure that green at today's base before starting — those scripts have moved again since 2026-08-21.

Dispatching to an `os-dev` at **opus**. Tier derived live, not recalled — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --tier scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs` at `e3f056fce`:

> Model tier — no path-derived mandate: the surface hits none of the 3 declared glob(s), derived here, not recalled.

So it is my judgment call, and I am taking opus rather than the sonnet floor for one reason: this card's failure mode is a dev who *diagnoses by reasoning*. The macOS root causes are unreachable from this lane, the temptation to explain them anyway is high, and a plausible-sounding wrong diagnosis written into a gate's verdict line is worse than the current opaque red.

Unblocked this round — `Blocked-by: #10611` discharged when #11538 merged. Scope and the ⛔ boundary are in the unlock comment above.

## Ruling: **A** — closing as fixed by #10275. No code lands, and none should.

PM decision on the dispatched dev's open question. I verified its central claims independently on `origin/main` before ruling:

```
scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs    isEntrypoint=2   raw argv compare=0
scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs      isEntrypoint=2   raw argv compare=0
scripts/invoked-as.mjs                     realpath mentions=5
.github/workflows/lint.yml:217             node scripts/invoked-as.mjs --self-test
.github/workflows/lint.yml:245             pnpm check:entry-guard

2e39181a7  2026-08-20T15:47:39Z
  "fix(scripts): route every entry guard through one symlink-correct predicate, and close the class (#10275)"
#10303 filed  2026-08-20T15:33:32Z          ⇒ the fix merged 14m07s after this card was filed
```

#10275's **own subject line names the symlink cause**. This card was filed fourteen minutes before the commit that closed exactly this class, and for four days nobody connected them — because the report framed the symptom as macOS, and every reader after that, including this seat, reasoned inside that frame.

## What this card actually was

Not a macOS portability bug. The pre-#10275 guard —

```js
if (resolve(process.argv[1] ?? '') === resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)))
```

— has no realpath leg, so a script reached through a **symlinked path** answers false, does nothing, and exits **0 with no output**. Both self-tests spawn fixtures under `os.tmpdir()`, so a symlinked TMPDIR is the whole trigger. macOS was a correlate, not a cause.

The reproduction is bit-exact on Linux across three independent axes — pre/post code, symlink vs plain TMPDIR, and a single-line ablation on today's tree — with exactly one red cell per script in the 2×2, so neither reading is vacuous. The ablated symlinked run reproduces this issue body **character-for-character**, including why `I2` has four assertions but only three go red (`--list` exiting 0 cannot distinguish "ran and succeeded" from "nothing ran" — predicted by the source comment at `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:3672`, and matching this report's own "3 failure(s)").

## ⛔ Why route A was correctly abandoned

I proposed declaring a Linux-only assumption in these two gates, mirroring #11538's `PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK`. **That route was wrong and the dev said so instead of imitating it.** There is no undetected Linux-only assumption here to declare; the assumption was symlink-freedom in the spawn path, and it is already fixed centrally in one predicate rather than declared in 142 places. Writing "this assumes Linux" into these verdict lines would have encoded a diagnosis this run measured to be **false** — precisely what my own dispatch called worse than the opaque red. My route did not transfer, and being told that is worth more than a compliant imitation of it.

**My filename lead was also wrong.** I argued `console-.md` and `objectui-digest-selftest-` looked like templates interpolating an empty value. They are redacted 12-hex shas, same redaction as `/var/folders/…` in the same string — disproved two ways (`head` comes from `execFileSync`, which throws rather than returning `''`; and the repro lands on the identical file and line with a demonstrably non-empty sha). It was still the right thing to chase: asking *who writes that filename* is what led to the entry guard.

## The discriminator worth keeping

In the failing run, `✓ the pin file is updated` **passes** while the three changeset checks fail. That is only possible if the bash driver ran to completion and resolved the sha — so only the **node child** went inert. One line separating "the shell broke" from "the guard went inert." Anyone debugging a silent-exit-0 gate should reach for that shape first.

## PM error, recorded

I graded this `pm:blocked` on #10611 and told the maintainer its unlock depended on an unanswered question — *"is macOS a host the fleet must support?"* **That question was never load-bearing for this card.** The blocked-chain was built on the report's framing, which I re-verified for accuracy but never for *relevance*. A cheaper move was available the whole time and I did not take it: re-run the failures against the report-era commit rather than only against today's `main`. Today's green told me "not reproducible"; the 2×2 tells you *why*, and the why is what closes the card.

## One unmeasured link — deliberately not blocking on it

Whether the reporter's macOS `os.tmpdir()` actually resolves through a symlink is **NOT MEASURED**; no macOS host in this lane, and the dev correctly declined to reason its way there. It does not change the disposition either way. One line for anyone on a Mac:

```
node -p "[require('os').tmpdir(), require('fs').realpathSync(require('os').tmpdir())]"
```

Two different strings confirms it. If it comes back identical, reopen this — the diagnosis would then be incomplete rather than wrong.

Also recorded, not filed: this issue's body says both gates sit in `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`; the digest is not in that script today. Issue-text slip, not a repo defect.

Closing `completed`. `pm:dispatched` stripped.
